correctness.rationale: The theorem fixes all quantifiers and metric conventions. Degree sequences force NODF invariance when a guild has at most two vertices, reducing the finite exclusion to 3-by-3 and 3-by-4 connected incidence matrices. In the actual packaged standard-library checker, all 2^(pa) incidence matrices are enumerated with BFS connectedness tests; it exhausts the 216 and 4320 directed connected checkerboard swaps at those sizes. Every NODF comparison is exact rational, and each maximum modularity is computed by exact subset-partition DP whose recurrence enumerates every set partition inductively. No smaller co-improvement occurs. The explicit connected 3-by-5 pair has NODF values 5/13 and 11/26 and optimized modularities 9/32 and 39/128. An independent restricted-growth partition iterator verifies both witness optima over all 4140 partitions. A finite proof is claimed only for the bounded threshold; no simulation supports an infinite inference.

value.rationale: Degree-preserving swaps are the canonical ecological network null-model move, and NODF and Newman–Girvan Q are widely used but competing measures of overlap and modular organization. The natural problem is whether strict local improvements can coexist while every species degree is fixed and networks stay connected, without confounding optimization artifacts. The result proves an exact minimum graph size, uses global integer optimization instead of heuristic modularity algorithms, and exhibits a tight connected unicyclic witness. This is a structurally motivated finite cutoff and reproducible benchmark, not an arbitrary slice or routine restatement of definitions. It does not claim ecological dynamical benefits.
